turns.content: Tell me about yourself and what specifically interests you in this Software Engineer Intern role.

I am a final year student. I built a hostel complaints portal that our warden actually uses now, it has around 150 complaints logged a month, built with React and Firebase. I am interested in this role because I enjoy the frontend side and want to work on a product people use daily.
What do you hope to learn or achieve during an internship with our company?
Honestly I just want to get good at writing production code. In college nobody reviews my code, so I want feedback from senior engineers.
Describe a challenging technical problem you've faced in a project. How did you approach it, and what was the outcome?

The hostel portal had a problem where two wardens could mark the same complaint resolved and it overwrote the notes. I added a Firestore transaction that checks the status before updating and shows a message if someone else already changed it. After that we had no more lost notes, and I learned about race conditions the hard way.
How do you usually approach learning a new programming language or framework?

Um, so, I think basically I just, like, start doing things, and then, like, if something breaks I look it up, and basically it works out, I mean it depends on the thing, but basically I learn by doing it, you know, like that.
Can you explain the differences between let, const, and var in JavaScript?
var, let and const are all the same really, they all just declare variables. The only difference is the name, I think const is faster because it is compiled differently.
What is asynchronous JavaScript, and can you provide an example of when you would use it?
Async is when you use setTimeout. Like if you want something to happen after two seconds.
What are the core concepts of React that you find most appealing for building user interfaces?

Components and the one-way data flow. In my portal the complaint list is one component and each complaint card is a child, and the state lives in the list, so when a status changes everything below updates and I never have to sync things manually.
How do you pass data from a parent component to a child component in React?
Through props, and if it goes many levels deep I used Context for the logged-in warden so I did not have to pass it through every component.
